# PART 8 — INDIAN SOILS

**UPPCS Priority: 🔴 VERY HIGH**

This is your **Indian Soils Ratta Booklet**. Focus on **soil type → origin → properties → distribution → crops → minerals/chemistry → erosion/conservation → UP-specific soils**.

No common traps, PYQ connections or self-test.

---

# 1. 🇮🇳 INDIAN SOILS — MASTER CLASSIFICATION

The major soil groups of India are:

1. **Alluvial Soil**
2. **Black Soil**
3. **Red & Yellow Soil**
4. **Laterite Soil**
5. **Arid/Desert Soil**
6. **Forest/Mountain Soil**
7. **Peaty & Marshy Soil**
8. **Saline & Alkaline Soil**

### 🔥 MASTER RATTA

> **Alluvial → River deposits**

> **Black → Basalt + Cotton**

> **Red → Iron**

> **Laterite → Leaching**

> **Arid → Desert**

> **Forest → Mountains**

> **Peaty → Organic matter + Waterlogging**

> **Saline → Excess salts**

---

# 2. 🌾 ALLUVIAL SOIL

Origin:

> **River-deposited sediments**

Major distribution:

> **Northern Plains**

Also found in:

> Coastal plains + river valleys + deltas.

Major rivers responsible:

> Indus

> Ganga

> Brahmaputra

> Mahanadi

> Godavari

> Krishna

> Kaveri.

### 🔴

> **Alluvial → Rivers → Plains**

---

# 3. 🌾 ALLUVIAL SOIL — DISTRIBUTION

Major states:

> Punjab

> Haryana

> Uttar Pradesh

> Bihar

> West Bengal

> Assam

Also:

> Rajasthan

> Gujarat

> Coastal/deltaic regions.

### 🔴

> **Ganga Plain → Alluvial soil**

---

# 4. 🌾 ALLUVIAL SOIL — CHARACTERISTICS

Generally:

> **Very fertile**

Texture:

> Sandy → loamy → clayey depending on location.

Rich in:

> Potash

> Lime

> Often adequate in phosphoric acid.

Generally deficient in:

> **Nitrogen**

> **Humus**

### 🔥

> **Alluvial → Fertile + river deposited + N deficient**

---

# 5. 🌾 ALLUVIAL SOIL — MAJOR CROPS

Important crops:

> **Rice**

> **Wheat**

> **Sugarcane**

> Maize

> Pulses

> Oilseeds

> Jute.

### 🔴

> **Alluvial → Rice + Wheat + Sugarcane**

---

# 6. 🌾 ALLUVIAL SOIL — TWO MAJOR TYPES

> **Bhangar**

> **Khadar**

### 🔥

> **Bhangar = Old alluvium**

> **Khadar = New alluvium**

---

# 7. 🌾 BHANGAR

Definition:

> **Older alluvial deposits**

Location:

> Relatively higher terraces above active floodplains.

Characteristics:

> Older

> Less frequently flooded

> Contains **kankar**.

### 🔴

> **Bhangar → Old → Kankar**

---

# 8. 🌾 KHADAR

Definition:

> **Newer alluvial deposits**

Location:

> Active floodplains.

Renewed by:

> Flood deposition.

Characteristics:

> Generally more fertile than Bhangar.

### 🔴

> **Khadar → New → Floodplain → Fertile**

---

# 9. 🧱 KANKAR

Composition:

> **Calcareous nodules**

Commonly associated with:

> **Bhangar**

### 🔴

> **Kankar → Bhangar**

---

# 10. 🌾 BHABAR–TERAI SOILS

### Bhabar

> Coarse sediments

> Highly porous

> Streams disappear underground.

### Terai

> Fine sediments

> Water re-emerges

> Marshy/wet.

### 🔥

> **Bhabar → Porous → Disappearing streams**

> **Terai → Water reappears → Wet**

---

# 11. ⚫ BLACK SOIL

Also called:

> **Regur soil**

Major origin:

> **Basaltic rocks**

Major region:

> **Deccan Plateau**

Major crop:

> **Cotton**

### 🔥 MASTER

> **Basalt → Black soil → Cotton**

---

# 12. ⚫ BLACK SOIL — DISTRIBUTION

Major states:

> Maharashtra

> Madhya Pradesh

> Gujarat

> Telangana

> Andhra Pradesh

> Karnataka

> Tamil Nadu.

Also:

> Parts of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

---

# 13. ⚫ BLACK SOIL — DECCAN REGION

Major areas:

> Maharashtra

> Western Madhya Pradesh

> Gujarat

> Telangana

> Northern Karnataka.

Geological association:

> **Deccan Traps**

### 🔴

> **Deccan Traps → Basalt → Black Soil**

---

# 14. ⚫ BLACK SOIL — COLOUR

Dark colour is associated with:

> Parent material + iron/magnesian minerals + organic matter in varying amounts.

Important:

> Black colour does **not** simply mean high humus.

---

# 15. ⚫ BLACK SOIL — TEXTURE

Characteristics:

> **Very fine clayey texture**

Major clay mineral:

> **Montmorillonite/smectite group**

Result:

> High swelling and shrinkage.

### 🔴

> **Black soil → Smectite → Swelling/shrinkage**

---

# 16. ⚫ BLACK SOIL — WATER RETENTION

Very high:

> **Moisture-holding capacity**

Reason:

> High clay content.

Therefore:

> Remains moist for relatively long periods.

### 🔴

> **Black soil → Clay → High moisture retention**

---

# 17. ⚫ BLACK SOIL — CRACKING

During dry season:

> Soil contracts.

Result:

> **Deep wide cracks**

This process:

> Helps natural aeration.

### 🔴

> **Black soil → Drying → Deep cracks**

---

# 18. ⚫ BLACK SOIL — SELF-PLOUGHING

Deep cracks:

> Open during dry season.

When wet:

> Soil expands.

Repeated:

> Shrinking + swelling

can create:

> **Self-ploughing effect**

### 🔴

> **Black soil → Shrink–swell → Self-ploughing**

---

# 19. ⚫ BLACK SOIL — CHEMICAL PROPERTIES

Generally rich in:

> Calcium

> Magnesium

> Iron

> Potash.

Generally poor in:

> **Nitrogen**

> **Phosphorus**

> **Humus/organic matter**

### 🔴

> **Black → Ca + Mg + Fe + K**

> **Black → N + P relatively deficient**

---

# 20. ⚫ BLACK SOIL — CROPS

Most famous:

> **Cotton**

Other crops:

> Soybean

> Wheat

> Sugarcane

> Groundnut

> Pulses

> Tobacco.

### 🔥

> **Black → Cotton**

---

# 21. 🔴 RED SOIL

Colour:

> **Iron compounds**

Parent material:

> Ancient crystalline/metamorphic rocks.

Major distribution:

> Peninsular India.

---

# 22. 🔴 RED SOIL — DISTRIBUTION

Important states:

> Tamil Nadu

> Karnataka

> Andhra Pradesh

> Telangana

> Odisha

> Chhattisgarh

> Jharkhand

> Maharashtra

> Madhya Pradesh.

Also:

> Parts of Uttar Pradesh.

### 🔴

> **Red soil → Peninsular India**

---

# 23. 🔴 RED SOIL — WHY RED?

Main reason:

> **Iron oxidation**

Iron:

> Ferric compounds

give:

> Red colour.

### 🔥

> **Red soil → Iron → Red colour**

---

# 24. 🟡 YELLOW SOIL

Red soil can appear:

> **Yellow**

when iron is present in:

> **Hydrated form**

### 🔴

> **Red → Iron oxidation**

> **Yellow → Hydrated iron compounds**

---

# 25. 🔴 RED SOIL — FERTILITY

Generally:

> **Less fertile than alluvial and black soils**

Often deficient in:

> Nitrogen

> Phosphorus

> Humus.

May require:

> Fertilisation for intensive agriculture.

---

# 26. 🔴 RED SOIL — CROPS

Major crops:

> Millets

> Pulses

> Groundnut

> Tobacco

> Cotton

> Potato

> Rice in suitable irrigated areas.

---

# 27. 🧱 LATERITE SOIL

Word origin:

> Latin **later = brick**

Formation:

> **High temperature + heavy rainfall**

Main process:

> **Leaching**

### 🔥

> **Heavy rain → Leaching → Laterite**

---

# 28. 🧱 LATERITE — LEACHING

Heavy rainfall:

> Dissolves soluble nutrients.

Downward movement:

> **Leaching**

Remaining relatively:

> Iron + aluminium.

### 🔴

> **Laterite → Leaching → Fe + Al**

---

# 29. 🧱 LATERITE — DISTRIBUTION

Major regions:

> Western Ghats

> Eastern Ghats

> Karnataka

> Kerala

> Tamil Nadu

> Odisha

> Jharkhand

> Chhattisgarh

> Northeast India.

### 🔴

> **Laterite → High rainfall areas**

---

# 30. 🧱 LATERITE — FERTILITY

Natural fertility:

> Generally **low**

Reason:

> Strong leaching removes nutrients.

Can become productive with:

> Fertilisation + proper management.

---

# 31. 🧱 LATERITE — CROPS

Under suitable management:

> Tea

> Coffee

> Rubber

> Cashew

> Coconut.

### 🔴

> **Laterite → Tea + Coffee + Rubber + Cashew**

---

# 32. 🧱 LATERITE — BUILDING USE

When exposed and hardened:

> Laterite can become:

> **Brick-like building material**

### 🔴

> **Laterite → Hardened → Building material**

---

# 33. 🏜️ ARID/DESERT SOIL

Major distribution:

> **Western Rajasthan**

Also:

> Gujarat

> Haryana

> Punjab

> dry parts of Deccan.

---

# 34. 🏜️ ARID SOIL — CHARACTERISTICS

Texture:

> Sandy

Colour:

> Red to brown.

Organic matter:

> Low.

Moisture:

> Low.

### 🔴

> **Arid soil → Sandy + low humus**

---

# 35. 🏜️ ARID SOIL — SALINITY

Because of:

> High evaporation

> Poor drainage in some locations

salts can accumulate.

### 🔴

> **Arid climate → High evaporation → Salt accumulation**

---

# 36. 🏜️ ARID SOIL — AGRICULTURE

With irrigation:

> Can support intensive agriculture.

Important crops:

> Wheat

> Bajra

> Barley

> Cotton

> Pulses.

### 🔴

> **Irrigation → Converts dry soils into productive agricultural land**

---

# 37. 🌲 FOREST/MOUNTAIN SOIL

Distribution:

> **Himalayan region**

Also:

> Other mountainous areas.

Characteristics depend on:

> Altitude

> Slope

> Vegetation

> Climate.

---

# 38. 🌲 MOUNTAIN SOIL — HUMUS

Under forest vegetation:

> Organic matter can accumulate.

Upper layers:

> Often rich in humus.

But:

> Steep slopes can cause erosion.

### 🔴

> **Mountain → Forest + slope → Humus + erosion**

---

# 39. 🌲 MOUNTAIN SOILS — ALTITUDE

At lower elevations:

> More suitable for agriculture.

Higher elevations:

> Forest/pastoral conditions.

Very high:

> Thin/immature soils.

### 🔴

> **Altitude ↑ → Soil development/vegetation changes**

---

# 40. 🌿 PEATY & MARSHY SOIL

Formation:

> **Waterlogged conditions**

Result:

> Slow decomposition of organic matter.

Therefore:

> **High organic matter**

Colour:

> Dark.

### 🔴

> **Waterlogging → Slow decomposition → Peaty soil**

---

# 41. 🌿 PEATY SOIL — DISTRIBUTION

Important regions:

> Kerala

> West Bengal

> Odisha

> Tamil Nadu

> Bihar and other wet lowlands.

---

# 42. 🌿 PEATY SOIL — CHEMISTRY

Characteristics:

> Rich in organic matter.

Often:

> Acidic.

May have:

> Poor drainage.

### 🔴

> **Peaty → Organic matter + waterlogging**

---

# 43. 🧂 SALINE & ALKALINE SOILS

Also called:

> **Usara soils** in parts of North India.

Major issue:

> Excess soluble salts / exchangeable sodium.

---

# 44. 🧂 SALINITY — CAUSES

Major causes:

> High evaporation

> Poor drainage

> Irrigation without adequate drainage

> Capillary rise of saline groundwater

> Arid/semi-arid climate.

### 🔥

> **Poor drainage + evaporation → Salinity**

---

# 45. 🧂 SALINE SOIL — DISTRIBUTION

Important areas:

> Rajasthan

> Gujarat

> Punjab

> Haryana

> Uttar Pradesh

> Maharashtra

> Coastal regions.

---

# 46. 🧂 ALKALINE SOIL

High:

> **Exchangeable sodium**

pH:

> Generally high.

Problem:

> Reduces soil productivity.

---

# 47. 🧂 RECLAMATION OF SALINE/ALKALINE SOILS

Methods:

> Proper drainage

> Leaching with good-quality water

> Gypsum for sodic soils

> Organic matter addition

> Improved irrigation management.

### 🔴

> **Sodic/alkaline soil → Gypsum**

---

# 48. 🌾 SOIL pH

### Acidic soil

> **pH < 7**

### Neutral

> **pH = 7**

### Alkaline

> **pH > 7**

### 🔴

> **pH ↓ → Acidity**

> **pH ↑ → Alkalinity**

---

# 49. 🧪 SOIL ACIDITY

Causes:

> Heavy rainfall

> Leaching of bases

> Organic acid accumulation.

Common in:

> High-rainfall regions.

### 🔴

> **Heavy rainfall → Leaching → Acidic tendency**

---

# 50. 🧪 SOIL ALKALINITY

Associated with:

> Sodium accumulation.

Common in:

> Dry/semi-arid + poorly drained regions.

### 🔴

> **Sodium accumulation → Alkalinity**

---

# 51. 🌾 SOIL FERTILITY

Soil fertility depends on:

> Nutrients

> Organic matter

> Water availability

> Soil structure

> Microorganisms

> pH

> Drainage.

### 🔴

> **Fertility ≠ simply nutrient quantity**

---

# 52. 🌱 PRIMARY PLANT NUTRIENTS

Major macronutrients:

> **Nitrogen (N)**

> **Phosphorus (P)**

> **Potassium (K)**

### 🔥

> **NPK → Primary macronutrients**

---

# 53. 🌱 SECONDARY NUTRIENTS

> **Calcium**

> **Magnesium**

> **Sulphur**

### 🔴

> **Ca + Mg + S → Secondary nutrients**

---

# 54. 🌱 MICRONUTRIENTS

Important:

> Iron

> Zinc

> Copper

> Manganese

> Boron

> Molybdenum

> Chlorine

> Nickel.

### 🔴

> **Micronutrient ≠ unimportant**

They are required:

> In very small quantities.

---

# 55. 🌱 NITROGEN

Importance:

> Vegetative growth

> Chlorophyll

> Protein synthesis.

Deficiency:

> Yellowing/chlorosis of older leaves.

### 🔴

> **N → Leaf/vegetative growth**

---

# 56. 🌱 PHOSPHORUS

Importance:

> Root development

> Energy transfer

> Flowering/seed formation.

### 🔴

> **P → Roots + energy + reproduction**

---

# 57. 🌱 POTASSIUM

Importance:

> Water regulation

> Enzyme activation

> Disease/stress resistance.

### 🔴

> **K → Water regulation + stress resistance**

---

# 58. 🧪 SOIL ORGANIC MATTER

Sources:

> Dead plants

> Animal residues

> Microbial biomass.

Importance:

> Soil structure

> Water retention

> Nutrient supply

> Microbial activity.

---

# 59. 🧪 HUMUS

Humus:

> Stable, decomposed organic matter.

Benefits:

> Improves soil structure.

> Increases water-holding capacity.

> Improves nutrient retention.

### 🔴

> **Humus → Organic matter + fertility + water retention**

---

# 60. 🌾 SOIL TEXTURE

Determined by relative proportion of:

> **Sand**

> **Silt**

> **Clay**

### 🔴

> **Texture → Sand + Silt + Clay**

---

# 61. 🏖️ SANDY SOIL

Characteristics:

> Large particles

> High drainage

> Low water retention.

### 🔴

> **Sand → Drainage high → Water retention low**

---

# 62. 🧱 CLAYEY SOIL

Characteristics:

> Very fine particles

> High water retention

> Poorer drainage.

### 🔴

> **Clay → Water retention high**

---

# 63. 🌾 LOAMY SOIL

Combination:

> Sand + silt + clay.

Generally:

> Good balance of drainage + moisture retention.

### 🔴

> **Loam → Balanced texture → Agriculture**

---

# 64. 🌊 SOIL EROSION

Definition:

> Removal of fertile topsoil by agents such as:

> **Water + wind**

Major agents:

> Running water

> Wind

> Glaciers

> Waves.

---

# 65. 🌧️ WATER EROSION

Major forms:

> Splash

> Sheet

> Rill

> Gully.

### 🔥

> **Sheet → Rill → Gully**

---

# 66. 🌧️ SHEET EROSION

Removal:

> Thin uniform layer of topsoil.

Occurs when:

> Surface runoff spreads over large area.

### 🔴

> **Sheet → Thin layer removed**

---

# 67. 🌧️ RILL EROSION

Runoff:

> Concentrates into small channels.

Result:

> **Small grooves/rills**

### 🔴

> **Rill → Small channels**

---

# 68. 🌊 GULLY EROSION

Rills:

> Become larger/deeper channels.

Result:

> **Gullies**

Severe form:

> Can create badlands/ravines.

### 🔴

> **Gully → Deep channels → Ravines**

---

# 69. 🏜️ CHAMBAL RAVINES

Major region:

> **Chambal Basin**

States:

> Madhya Pradesh + Rajasthan + Uttar Pradesh.

Cause:

> **Severe gully erosion**

### 🔥

> **Chambal → Ravines → Gully erosion**

---

# 70. 🌬️ WIND EROSION

Major region:

> **Rajasthan**

Occurs through:

> Deflation

> Abrasion

> Saltation.

### 🔴

> **Wind erosion → Arid/semi-arid regions**

---

# 71. 🌬️ DESERTIFICATION

Definition:

> Land degradation in drylands.

Causes:

> Vegetation loss

> Overgrazing

> Deforestation

> Unsustainable agriculture

> Water mismanagement

> Climate variability.

---

# 72. 🌳 SOIL CONSERVATION

Major methods:

> Afforestation

> Contour ploughing

> Terrace farming

> Strip cropping

> Shelterbelts

> Check dams

> Gully plugging

> Crop rotation.

---

# 73. 🏔️ CONTOUR PLOUGHING

Ploughing:

> **Along contour lines**

Purpose:

> Reduce runoff velocity.

Suitable for:

> Sloping land.

### 🔴

> **Contour → Slope → Reduce runoff**

---

# 74. 🏔️ TERRACE FARMING

Slopes are converted into:

> **Step-like terraces**

Purpose:

> Reduce runoff + soil erosion.

Common:

> Hilly regions.

### 🔴

> **Terraces → Mountains/slopes**

---

# 75. 🌾 STRIP CROPPING

Crops:

> Planted in strips.

Purpose:

> Reduce wind/water erosion.

Useful:

> Semi-arid/agricultural areas.

---

# 76. 🌳 SHELTERBELTS

Rows of:

> Trees/shrubs

Purpose:

> Reduce wind speed.

Used mainly for:

> **Wind erosion control**

### 🔴

> **Shelterbelt → Wind erosion**

---

# 77. 🌳 AFFORESTATION

Planting trees on:

> Degraded/bare land.

Benefits:

> Reduces erosion

> Improves infiltration

> Adds organic matter

> Stabilises soil.

---

# 78. 🌊 CHECK DAMS

Small structures across:

> Drainage channels.

Purpose:

> Slow runoff

> Trap sediment

> Increase groundwater recharge.

### 🔴

> **Check dam → Runoff ↓ + sediment trapping**

---

# 79. 🧱 SOIL PROFILE

Typical soil profile:

> **O → A → B → C → R**

### O

> Organic layer

### A

> Topsoil

### B

> Subsoil

### C

> Parent material

### R

> Bedrock

### 🔥

> **O → A → B → C → R**

---

# 80. 🌱 TOPSOIL

Mainly:

> **A horizon**

Contains:

> Minerals + organic matter + biological activity.

Most important for:

> Agriculture.

### 🔴

> **Topsoil → A horizon**

---

# 81. 🧱 SUBSOIL

Mainly:

> **B horizon**

Characteristics:

> Accumulation of materials leached from upper horizons.

### 🔴

> **B horizon → Subsoil**

---

# 82. 🧱 PARENT MATERIAL

Mainly:

> **C horizon**

Represents:

> Weathered parent material.

### 🔴

> **C → Parent material**

---

# 83. 🪨 BEDROCK

> **R horizon**

Underlying:

> Solid rock.

### 🔴

> **R → Bedrock**

---

# 84. 🇮🇳 SOIL → PARENT ROCK

| Soil     | Major association             |
| -------- | ----------------------------- |
| Alluvial | River sediments               |
| Black    | Basalt                        |
| Red      | Crystalline/metamorphic rocks |
| Laterite | Strongly weathered rocks      |
| Arid     | Desert deposits               |
| Mountain | Parent rocks + organic matter |

---

# 85. 🇮🇳 SOIL → CLIMATE

| Soil     | Climatic association       |
| -------- | -------------------------- |
| Alluvial | River plains               |
| Black    | Semi-arid/sub-humid Deccan |
| Red      | Warm Peninsular regions    |
| Laterite | Hot + wet                  |
| Arid     | Hot + dry                  |
| Forest   | Mountain climates          |
| Peaty    | Wet/waterlogged            |

---

# 86. 🇮🇳 SOIL → CROP

### Alluvial

> Rice + Wheat + Sugarcane + Jute

### Black

> Cotton + Soybean

### Red

> Millets + Groundnut + Pulses

### Laterite

> Tea + Coffee + Rubber + Cashew

### Arid

> Bajra + Wheat with irrigation

### 🔥

> **Black → Cotton**

> **Laterite → Tea/Coffee**

> **Alluvial → Rice/Wheat/Sugarcane**

---

# 87. 🇮🇳 SOIL → CHEMISTRY

### Alluvial

> Potash + Lime generally adequate

### Black

> Ca + Mg + Fe + K

### Red

> Iron-rich

### Laterite

> Fe + Al

### Peaty

> Organic matter-rich

### Saline

> Soluble salts

### Alkaline/Sodic

> Sodium-rich

---

# 88. 🌾 SOIL FERTILITY — BROAD ORDER

Generally:

> **Alluvial → Highly productive**

> **Black → Highly productive under suitable conditions**

> **Red → Moderate/low naturally**

> **Laterite → Low naturally**

> **Arid → Low naturally**

> **Peaty → Variable**

> **Saline/alkaline → Poor until reclaimed**

---

# 89. 🇮🇳 INDIAN SOILS — REGIONAL MAP

### Northern India

> **Alluvial**

### Deccan

> **Black**

### Eastern/Southern Peninsula

> **Red**

### High rainfall Western Ghats

> **Laterite**

### Western Rajasthan

> **Arid**

### Himalayas

> **Mountain/forest**

### Wetlands

> **Peaty/marshy**

### Irrigated drylands/coastal areas

> **Saline/alkaline**

---

# 90. 🗺️ UTTAR PRADESH — SOILS

UP is dominated by:

> **Alluvial soils**

Major soil regions include:

> **Bhangar**

> **Khadar**

> **Red soils**

> **Black soils**

> **Alluvial variations**

> **Saline/alkaline soils**

---

# 91. 🌾 UP — ALLUVIAL SOIL

Dominant:

> **Ganga–Yamuna Plain**

Major regions:

> Almost the entire central and northern plains.

Importance:

> Agriculture.

Major crops:

> Wheat

> Rice

> Sugarcane

> Pulses

> Oilseeds.

### 🔥

> **UP → Ganga Plain → Alluvial**

---

# 92. 🌾 UP — BHANGAR

Found:

> Older alluvial terraces.

Associated:

> **Kankar**

### 🔴

> **UP Bhangar → Old alluvium + Kankar**

---

# 93. 🌾 UP — KHADAR

Found:

> Floodplains of major rivers.

Major:

> Ganga

> Yamuna

> Ghaghara

> Gomti etc.

Characteristics:

> Newer alluvium.

### 🔴

> **UP Khadar → River floodplains**

---

# 94. 🔴 UP — RED SOIL

Found mainly:

> **Southern/eastern plateau areas**

Associated with:

> Vindhyan region.

Important districts/areas:

> Mirzapur

> Sonbhadra

> adjoining Bundelkhand/Vindhyan region.

> **Southern UP → Red soil**

---

# 95. ⚫ UP — BLACK SOIL

Found:

> **Bundelkhand region**

Especially:

> Southern UP.

Association:

> Black/vertic soils in parts of Bundelkhand.

### 🔴

> **Bundelkhand → Black soil association**

---

# 96. 🧂 UP — USAR SOIL

Term:

> **Usar**

Associated with:

> Saline/alkaline/sodic soils.

Major occurrence:

> Gangetic plain.

Problem:

> Poor agricultural productivity.

### 🔥

> **Usar → Sodic/alkaline soil → UP**

---

# 97. 🧂 UP — SOIL RECLAMATION

Important:

> **Gypsum**

Used especially for:

> **Sodic/alkali soils**

Other methods:

> Drainage

> Irrigation management

> Organic amendments

> Salt-tolerant crops.

### 🔴

> **UP Usar → Gypsum reclamation**

---

# 98. 🌾 UP — SOIL → REGION

| Region             | Major soil               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ |
| Western UP         | Alluvial                 |
| Central UP         | Alluvial                 |
| Eastern UP         | Alluvial                 |
| Terai              | Alluvial/wet soils       |
| Bundelkhand        | Red + black associations |
| Vindhyan/Sonbhadra | Red/forest-related soils |
| Sodic patches      | Usar                     |

# 99. 🔥 INDIAN SOILS — MASTER TABLE

| Soil               | Origin/feature              | Major region                | Main association |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------- |
| **Alluvial**       | River deposits              | Northern Plains             | Rice/Wheat       |
| **Black**          | Basalt                      | Deccan                      | Cotton           |
| **Red**            | Iron-rich crystalline rocks | Peninsula                   | Millets          |
| **Laterite**       | Leaching                    | High rainfall areas         | Tea/Coffee       |
| **Arid**           | Desert deposits             | Rajasthan                   | Bajra            |
| **Mountain**       | Altitude/forest             | Himalayas                   | Forest           |
| **Peaty**          | Waterlogging                | Wetlands                    | Organic matter   |
| **Saline**         | Salt accumulation           | Dry/coastal/irrigated areas | Reclamation      |
| **Sodic/Alkaline** | Sodium accumulation         | UP etc.                     | Gypsum           |

---

# 100. 🔥 BLACK SOIL — COMPLETE RATTA

> **Regur = Black soil**

> **Deccan Traps → Basalt**

> **Basalt → Black soil**

> **Black soil → Smectite**

> **Smectite → Swelling**

> **Swelling + shrinking → Deep cracks**

> **Deep cracks → Self-ploughing**

> **Black soil → High moisture retention**

> **Black soil → Cotton**

> **Black soil → Ca + Mg + Fe + K**

> **Black soil → N + P relatively deficient**

---

# 101. 🔥 ALLUVIAL — COMPLETE RATTA

> **River deposition → Alluvial**

> **Northern Plains → Alluvial**

> **Bhangar → Old**

> **Khadar → New**

> **Bhangar → Kankar**

> **Khadar → Floodplain**

> **Alluvial → Fertile**

> **Alluvial → Rice + Wheat + Sugarcane**

---

# 102. 🔥 RED SOIL — COMPLETE RATTA

> **Peninsular India → Red soil**

> **Iron oxidation → Red**

> **Hydrated iron → Yellow**

> **Red soil → Crystalline/metamorphic rocks**

> **Red soil → Nitrogen/phosphorus/humus generally low**

> **Red soil → Millets + pulses + groundnut**

---

# 103. 🔥 LATERITE — COMPLETE RATTA

> **Hot + wet → Laterite**

> **Heavy rainfall → Leaching**

> **Leaching → Nutrient loss**

> **Fe + Al → Lateritic enrichment**

> **Laterite → Western Ghats + Northeast + parts of Peninsula**

> **Laterite → Tea + Coffee + Rubber + Cashew**

> **Hardened laterite → Building material**

---

# 104. 🔥 ARID SOIL — COMPLETE RATTA

> **Western Rajasthan → Arid soil**

> **Sandy → Low water retention**

> **Low rainfall → Low organic matter**

> **High evaporation → Salt accumulation**

> **Irrigation → Agricultural productivity can increase**

---

# 105. 🔥 PEATY SOIL — COMPLETE RATTA

> **Waterlogging → Peaty**

> **Slow decomposition → Organic matter accumulation**

> **Peaty → Dark**

> **Peaty → Wetlands**

> **Peaty → High organic matter**

---

# 106. 🔥 SALINE/SODIC SOIL — COMPLETE RATTA

> **Poor drainage → Salt accumulation**

> **High evaporation → Salinity**

> **Sodium → Sodic/alkaline soil**

> **High pH → Alkalinity**

> **Gypsum → Sodic soil reclamation**

> **Drainage → Essential for reclamation**

> **Usar → UP alkaline/sodic soil**

---

# 107. 🌱 SOIL EROSION — MASTER CHAIN

### Water

> **Splash → Sheet → Rill → Gully → Ravine**

### Wind

> **Deflation + Abrasion + Saltation**

### Conservation

> **Contour → Terrace → Strip → Shelterbelt → Afforestation**

---

# 108. 🌊 SOIL EROSION — ONE-LINE RATTA

> **Sheet → Uniform thin removal**

> **Rill → Small channels**

> **Gully → Deep channels**

> **Ravine → Advanced gully erosion**

> **Chambal → Ravines**

> **Rajasthan → Wind erosion**

---

# 109. 🌱 SOIL CONSERVATION — ONE-LINE RATTA

> **Contour ploughing → Slope**

> **Terracing → Hills**

> **Strip cropping → Erosion control**

> **Shelterbelts → Wind**

> **Afforestation → Vegetation cover**

> **Check dams → Runoff**

> **Gully plugging → Gully erosion**

> **Crop rotation → Soil fertility**

---
